summary: Built in 1935 on the Payette National Forest, this L-4 tower remains staffed and drive-up accessible, with staffing records limited to two documented years.

access.note: Active, drive-up accessible, seasonally staffed Forest Service lookout; not a public rental.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

events.note: R1/L-4 cab constructed on a 30-foot open timber tower.
Staffed by "Scoop" McCoy, per the Post Register.
Staffed by Leonard Mooney, per the Adams County Record.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, September 29, 2020, as US 1434, nominated by Brad Eells.

evidence.supports: Built 1935, R1/L-4 cab on 30-foot open timber tower.
evidence.quote: The lookout at Horse Mountain was constructed in 1935. An R1/L-4 cabin on a 30 foot open timber tower.

Drive-Up Staffed Elevation: 6892' Payette National Forest

notes_for_editor: Staffing history is thin — only two documented years (1939, 1981) across both sources checked, with a large undocumented gap in between. firelookout.com (not cited, consistent with others) also lists it as built 1935, 30-foot timber tower, staffed every summer, confirming the other two sources without adding new facts.
